# Hollerau Pumpenwerke - procurement data package v1.0.0

You are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, a fictional pump maker (start with
`company.md`). Everything is as of **2026-09-30**. Company data is synthetic; market series are real
open data (`ATTRIBUTION.md`). All company names are fictional; any match with a real company is
coincidental.

## Files
- `data/*.csv` - the master copy (UTF-8, comma, ISO dates, dot decimals); schema in `datapackage.json`.
- `world.sqlite` - the same tables in one SQLite file, generated from the CSVs.
- `facts.json` - every ID you can cite in a claim, with the values the arena checks.
- Prices are per `price_unit` (1, 100 or 1,000 pieces, kg or m), as the ERP states them; cases
  negotiate in the same unit.
- `company.md`, `SCORECARD.md`, `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, `ATTRIBUTION.md`; contract texts in `contracts/`,
  letters, e-mails and notes in `correspondence/`.

## IDs
`<type>:<id>[@period]`, unique across the package, in the first column of each table: `sup:70110`,
`part:310010`, `po:4500010001-10`, `gr:`, `inv:`, `qn:`, `ctr:4600070110` (clause `ctr:4600070110#3.1`),
`quote:`, `rfq:`, `fc:310010@2026-09`, `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `cost:310010`,
`news:`, `doc:`.

## Tables
| Table | Rows | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `suppliers` | 447 | Vendor master: the detailed suppliers (`detail = full`) and the long tail (`spend only`). |
| `supplier_intel` | 46 | Public face of each detailed supplier: register facts, filed turnover, credit index, audit. |
| `parts` | 60 | Material master of the detailed parts. |
| `sourcing` | 90 | Source list: approved suppliers per part, quota, tooling owner. |
| `price_conditions` | 339 | Price history per part and supplier (price per `price_unit`), with the event behind it. |
| `negotiation_history` | 300 | Past price events: renewals with asked and settled change. |
| `contracts` | 46 | Framework agreements (text in `contracts/`). |
| `contract_clauses` | 280 | Clauses of the framework agreements, incl. index clauses (`ctr:<no>#<clause>`). |
| `po_lines` | 5400 | Purchase order lines: requested and first confirmed date, price per `price_unit`. |
| `goods_receipts` | 5580 | Goods receipts per PO line (posting date, quantity). |
| `invoices` | 5578 | Supplier invoices with due and payment dates, cash discount taken. |
| `quality_notifications` | 1033 | Complaints against suppliers (QN), with 8D dates and recharged fees. |
| `scorecards` | 414 | Rolling 12-month supplier scorecards per quarter (method: `SCORECARD.md`). |
| `forecasts` | 720 | Quarterly demand forecast snapshots per part, shared with suppliers. |
| `forecast_lines` | 8640 | Monthly quantities of each forecast snapshot. |
| `rfqs` | 47 | Requests for quotation: past benchmarks, second-source quotes, open RFQs for new parts. |
| `quotes` | 108 | Supplier quotes (price per `price_unit`); missing fields as the supplier sent them. |
| `spend_cube` | 1137 | Spend per fiscal year and supplier, incl. the long tail. |
| `index_series` | 33 | Market series: source, licence, unit; derived series with their formula. |
| `index_values` | 2258 | Monthly values of the market series (`idx:<series>@<YYYY-MM>`). |
| `cost_drivers` | 166 | The category team's estimate of each part's cost drivers (index series and weight). |
| `should_cost` | 28 | Bottom-up should-cost estimates for selected parts (`cost:<part>`). |
| `news` | 39 | Press items about suppliers and markets. |
| `documents` | 208 | Letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes (text in `correspondence/`). |

## How the tables connect
```
suppliers 1-n sourcing n-1 parts          parts 1-n price_conditions n-1 suppliers
suppliers 1-1 supplier_intel, 1-n contracts 1-n contract_clauses
po_lines -> goods_receipts -> invoices;   goods_receipts 1-n quality_notifications
parts 1-n forecasts 1-n forecast_lines;   rfqs 1-n quotes;   index_series 1-n index_values
suppliers -> scorecards, spend_cube, news, documents;   parts -> cost_drivers, should_cost
```

## Example queries (SQLite)
```sql
-- spend by supplier, last fiscal year
SELECT s.name, c.spend_eur FROM spend_cube c JOIN suppliers s ON s.id = c.supplier_id
WHERE c.fiscal_year = 'FY2026' ORDER BY c.spend_eur DESC LIMIT 10;
-- price history of one part
SELECT supplier_id, valid_from, price, price_unit FROM price_conditions WHERE part_id = 'part:310010';
-- latest scorecard per supplier
SELECT supplier_id, otd_pct, ppm, colour FROM scorecards WHERE quarter = '2026Q3' ORDER BY score;
-- an index over the last year
SELECT month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-C2451' AND month >= '2025-08';
-- how late Hollerau pays a supplier
SELECT AVG(julianday(paid_date) - julianday(due_date)) FROM invoices
WHERE supplier_id = 'sup:70210' AND discount_taken = 0 AND paid_date IS NOT NULL;
```
# Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH

Family-owned pump maker from Hollerau, Lower Bavaria, Germany, founded 1952, owned by the Stangl family (third generation). Revenue about
EUR 252 M, 910 employees, one plant. Fiscal year October to September.

## Products
- **HN**: HN standard water pumps (EN 733)
- **HB**: HB building-services inline pumps
- **HI**: HI industrial process pumps, stainless (ISO 5199)
- **HX**: HX high-efficiency series (start of production 2027-03)

## Purchasing
You are the purchasing team for the pump line's parts and materials (about EUR 35 M in FY2026, see
`spend_cube.csv`). The detailed data covers the 46 suppliers and 60 parts that matter most.

## Policies
- Standard payment terms: 60 days net. Cost of capital for valuing payment terms:
  8% a year.
- Approval: deals above EUR 250 k a year need the head of purchasing, above EUR 1 M the managing director.
- A-parts are dual-sourced where a qualified second source exists (`sourcing.csv`).
- Quality agreement with every series supplier: on-time delivery target 95 %, flat fee of
  EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint, 8D report within 60 days.
- Preferred Incoterm: DAP Hollerau. Freight for EXW/FCA deliveries is booked by Hollerau.

## Should-cost
`should_cost.csv` estimates full cost without margin. For the parts of strategic and bottleneck
negotiations the category team modelled the current supplier's own plant (`supplier_id`, error about
5 %); the other rows use a German cost base with an error of 5-15 %. Rule of thumb for other countries'
full cost relative to Germany: AT and CH about 1.0-1.1, CZ, PL and HU about 0.8-0.85, TR about 0.75,
CN about 0.7.

## Category strategies
Every negotiation states its category goal (`stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage`, `routine`); the rates of its cost C follow it.
Quality escalations are `quality_first`, capacity squeezes `secure_supply`, kits and bundles `routine`.

| Category | Strategy | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| castings | secure supply and energy-cost transparency; build Central-European second sources | stabilise |
| machined parts | leverage: competition between local job shops, bundle small parts | leverage |
| sheet metal | leverage; quality first after the 2026 base-frame issues | leverage |
| seals | bottleneck: long-term agreements, qualify second sources where approvals allow | secure_supply |
| electrical | strategic: copper and electronics clauses, multi-year frameworks | stabilise |
| C-parts | routine: fewer suppliers, kits, lower process cost | routine |
| raw material | index-based pricing, negotiate base price and extras | leverage |

## Targets for FY2027
Material cost -3 % against the index-adjusted baseline; no supplier in red for more than two quarters.
# Known issues

The data is shaped like a real ERP extract, quirks included. None of these are errors to report.

1. Three delivery dates per PO line: requested, first confirmed and the goods-receipt posting date. OTD
   differs by 10-30 points depending on the reference date.
2. Goods receipts are posted on working days only (weekends, Bavarian holidays, August shutdown).
3. Partial deliveries (two receipts per line) and small over-deliveries within 5 %.
4. C-parts, some raw material and the motor cable are priced per 100 or per 1,000 units (`price_unit`);
   a PO line's value is qty x price / price_unit.
5. One supplier sits twice in the vendor master: `sup:71999` is the old record of `sup:70210` (renamed 2024).
6. A few PO lines use an outdated price (`price_note = stale_condition`): purchase price variance.
7. Index clauses are in `contract_clauses.csv` and in the contract text (`contracts/`).
8. Past quotes miss fields where the supplier left them out (`missing_fields`).
9. Invoices are paid late for some suppliers; a few cash discounts were taken after the discount period.
10. Complaints on small lots make PPM jumpy; read the rolling scorecard, not single lots.
11. PO lines with requested dates after 2026-09-30 are open orders without receipts.
12. Index series end at different months: each source publishes with its own lag (`index_series.csv`).
13. Small suppliers file no profit and loss account: `supplier_intel.csv` gives their turnover as a band.
14. Should-cost (`should_cost.csv`) assumes a German cost base and has an error of 5-15 %.
15. The spend cube holds about 400 further suppliers known only by name, category and spend.
# Supplier scorecard - method

Each row (`sc:<supplier>@<quarter>`) covers the rolling 12 months to the end of that quarter and is sent to
the supplier, so both sides know it.

- **otd_pct**: share of goods-receipt lines posted between 5 days before and 2 days after the
  requested date of the PO line. **otd_confirmed_pct**: the same against the supplier's first confirmed date.
  Partial deliveries count as separate lines.
- **ppm**: supplier-caused complaint quantity / received quantity x 1,000,000 (complaints by date of the QN).
- **open_8d_overdue**: supplier-caused complaints older than 60 days without a closed 8D report at quarter end.
- **score** = 0.5 x otd_pct + 0.5 x quality points - 5 x open_8d_overdue, with quality points =
  100 x max(0, 1 - ppm / 10,000).
- **class / colour**: A green >= 85, B amber 70-84.9, C red < 70.

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

"""The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.

C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
not in the language model.
"""

import math
import operator
from datetime import date

# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
OPS = {
    "<=": operator.le,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    ">": operator.gt,
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
}


def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""
    b, t = case["buyer"], closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")
    years = _years(case, t)
    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years
    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
    index = index_risk = 0.0
    if clause := t.get("index_clause"):
        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
    return {
        "price": spend,
        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
        "index_clause": index,
        "index_risk": index_risk,
        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),
    }


def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for terms without a price (e.g. a supplier that quotes none), so such a
    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:
        return math.inf
    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)


def score(c_open, c_deal, c_best):
    if c_deal is None:
        return 0.0
    if c_open - c_best <= 0.01:  # no room to negotiate: matching the best is full marks
        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))


def must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard=None):
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []):
        value = t.get(m["field"])
        if value is None and m["op"] not in ("==", "!="):
            return False
        if not OPS[m["op"]](value, m["value"]):
            return False
    return True


def snap(case, field, value):
    """The allowed value closest to `value` (case `term_options`), else `value` unchanged."""
    options = case.get("term_options", {}).get(field)
    if not options or value in options:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and all(isinstance(o, int | float) for o in options):
        return min(options, key=lambda o: (abs(o - value), o))
    return options[0]


def complete_offer(case, terms):
    """A valid term sheet: exactly the negotiable fields, gaps from the buyer's plan, snapped."""
    plan = closing_terms(case, {"unit_price": None})
    freight = case["buyer"]["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan["incoterm"] = min(freight, key=freight.get)  # when asking, ask for the cheapest freight
    out = {}
    for field in case["negotiable"]:
        value = terms.get(field, plan.get(field))
        if value is None and case.get("term_options", {}).get(field):
            value = case["term_options"][field][0]
        value = snap(case, field, value)
        out[field] = round(value, 2) if field == "unit_price" and value is not None else value
    return out

Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.296/c5a74becea7af90349db2ab2e4d4f721/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |

"""Data package exploration: supplier profiles, persona signals, price fairness, case triggers.

Run: uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py [data/package]
Writes analysis/out/*.csv and analysis/out/explore.json (input for the report page).
"""

import json
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

PKG = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "data/package")
OUT = Path(__file__).parent / "out"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
db = sqlite3.connect(PKG / "world.sqlite")


def q(sql):
    return pd.read_sql_query(sql, db)


# Persona signals in call notes, meeting notes and e-mails. The generator writes each trait with
# one or two fixed phrasings, so plain patterns classify every note.
SIGNALS = {
    "cash_need": r"pay earlier|bank is watching|cash and the banks|within 10 days",
    "spare_capacity": r"second shift has been on hold|take additional parts",
    "capacity_full": r"order intake is very strong|binding 12-month commitment|cannot confirm your full forecast",
    "open_book": r"walk us through their calculation",
    "stale_costing": r"not followed his material|own spreadsheet",
    "partnership_2022": r"kept supplying at the old price",
    "reference_customer": r"important reference customer",
    "approval_2pct": r"above 2 % need the approval",
    "deprioritising_us": r"reviewing small accounts|not strategic|reorganising our range",
    "price_frozen": r"no room on price|not discounted|price list applies to all",
    "hedged": r"bought their \w+ forward|covered at fixed prices",
    "complains_late_pay": r"invoices are overdue",
}
LEVER = {
    "cash_need": "pay faster (14-30 days) for price; it values cash over list price",
    "spare_capacity": "offer volume / extra parts; idle capacity makes a lower price cheap for it",
    "capacity_full": "trade a firm 12-24 month commitment for price and allocation",
    "open_book": "ask for the cost breakdown XLSX, argue line by line vs should-cost",
    "stale_costing": "index data disarms it: show the real index path since its last price",
    "partnership_2022": "acknowledge 2022, frame the deal as partnership; avoid hard threats",
    "reference_customer": "it values the reference: tone and long-term framing move it",
    "approval_2pct": "keep each move small (2 % or less) or give it time for its committee",
    "deprioritising_us": "weak leverage: bundle volume, or use the alternative",
    "price_frozen": "price will not move: trade payment days, logistics, call-off flexibility",
    "hedged": "market index arguments are 'not our reality' until its hedge ends",
    "complains_late_pay": "our late payment hurt trust: promise and keep payment terms",
}


def notes():
    docs = q("SELECT id, date, kind, supplier_id, subject, file FROM documents")
    rows = []
    for d in docs.itertuples():
        text = (PKG / d.file).read_text()
        body = " ".join(text.splitlines()[4:]).strip()
        hits = [k for k, pat in SIGNALS.items() if re.search(pat, body, re.I)]
        rows.append({**d._asdict(), "body": body, "signals": hits})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def supplier_profiles(docs):
    sup = q("""
        SELECT s.id, s.name, s.country, s.category, s.payment_days, s.skonto_days, s.skonto_pct,
               s.incoterm, s.abc_class, i.owner_type, i.group_parent, i.staff, i.turnover_eur,
               i.turnover_band, i.equity_ratio_pct, i.credit_index, i.credit_index_12m_ago,
               i.vda63_grade
        FROM suppliers s JOIN supplier_intel i ON i.supplier_id = s.id WHERE s.detail = 'full'""")
    spend = q("""SELECT supplier_id id, spend_eur spend_fy26 FROM spend_cube WHERE fiscal_year='FY2026'""")
    spend = spend.groupby("id", as_index=False).sum()
    sc = q("""SELECT supplier_id id, otd_pct, otd_confirmed_pct, ppm, score, colour, open_8d_overdue
              FROM scorecards WHERE quarter='2026Q3'""")
    trend = q("""SELECT supplier_id id, group_concat(colour, '>') colour_trend
                 FROM (SELECT * FROM scorecards ORDER BY quarter) GROUP BY supplier_id""")
    # How late Hollerau pays, last 12 months (sup:71999 is the old record of sup:70210)
    pay = q("""
        SELECT CASE supplier_id WHEN 'sup:71999' THEN 'sup:70210' ELSE supplier_id END id,
               AVG(julianday(paid_date) - julianday(due_date)) days_late,
               AVG(julianday(paid_date) - julianday(due_date) > 5) share_late
        FROM invoices WHERE paid_date IS NOT NULL AND discount_taken = 0 AND invoice_date >= '2025-10-01'
        GROUP BY 1""")
    neg = q("""SELECT supplier_id id, COUNT(*) renewals, AVG(asked_pct) avg_asked,
                      AVG(settled_pct) avg_settled, AVG(asked_pct - settled_pct) avg_give
               FROM negotiation_history WHERE type = 'annual renewal' GROUP BY 1""")
    news = q("SELECT supplier_id id, group_concat(topic, ', ') news FROM news GROUP BY 1")
    sig = docs.explode("signals").dropna(subset=["signals"])
    sig = sig.groupby("supplier_id")["signals"].apply(lambda s: sorted(set(s))).rename("signals")
    p = sup
    for t in (spend, sc, trend, pay, neg, news):
        p = p.merge(t, on="id", how="left")
    p = p.merge(sig, left_on="id", right_index=True, how="left")
    p["signals"] = p["signals"].apply(lambda s: s if isinstance(s, list) else [])
    p["credit_change"] = p["credit_index"] - p["credit_index_12m_ago"]  # higher index = worse
    return p.sort_values("spend_fy26", ascending=False)


def price_fairness():
    """Per part and incumbent: current price, should-cost margin, index-implied change since the
    current price took effect, and what the supplier asks (trigger letters)."""
    cur = q("""
        SELECT pc.part_id, pc.supplier_id, pc.price, pc.price_unit, pc.valid_from, p.description,
               p.category, p.abc_class, s.country
        FROM price_conditions pc JOIN parts p ON p.id = pc.part_id JOIN suppliers s ON s.id = pc.supplier_id
        WHERE pc.valid_from = (SELECT MAX(valid_from) FROM price_conditions x
                               WHERE x.part_id = pc.part_id AND x.supplier_id = pc.supplier_id
                               AND x.valid_from <= '2026-09-30')""")
    sc = q("""SELECT part_id, supplier_id sc_supplier, cost_base, unit_cost, price_unit sc_unit,
                     confidence_pct FROM should_cost""")
    # Country factor for German-base should-cost (company.md rule of thumb, midpoints)
    factor = {"DE": 1.0, "AT": 1.05, "CH": 1.05, "CZ": 0.825, "PL": 0.825, "HU": 0.825, "TR": 0.75, "CN": 0.7}
    df = cur.merge(sc, on="part_id", how="left")
    own = df["sc_supplier"].notna()
    df = df[~own | (df["sc_supplier"] == df["supplier_id"])]
    df["full_cost_est"] = df["unit_cost"] * df["price_unit"] / df["sc_unit"]
    df.loc[~own, "full_cost_est"] *= df.loc[~own, "country"].map(factor).fillna(1.0)
    df["margin_pct"] = (df["price"] - df["full_cost_est"]) / df["price"] * 100

    # Index-implied change: cost-driver weights x index move from the month before the current
    # price took effect to each series' latest month.
    drivers = q("SELECT part_id, series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers")
    iv = q("SELECT series_id, month, value FROM index_values")
    last = iv.sort_values("month").groupby("series_id").last()
    moves = []
    for r in df.itertuples():
        ref_month = pd.Period(r.valid_from, "M") - 1
        tot = 0.0
        for d in drivers[drivers.part_id == r.part_id].itertuples():
            s = iv[(iv.series_id == d.series_id) & (iv.month <= str(ref_month))]
            if s.empty:
                continue
            tot += d.weight * (last.loc[d.series_id, "value"] / s.iloc[-1]["value"] - 1)
        moves.append(tot * 100)
    df["index_move_pct"] = moves
    return df


def triggers(docs, prof, fair):
    t = q("""SELECT id, date, kind, supplier_id, part_ids, subject, asked_pct, asked_price,
                    effective_date FROM documents WHERE id LIKE '%-P__' ORDER BY id""")
    t["case"] = t["id"].str[-3:]
    rows = []
    for r in t.itertuples():
        parts = (r.part_ids or "").split(";")
        f = fair[(fair.supplier_id == r.supplier_id) & (fair.part_id.isin(parts))]
        p = prof[prof.id == r.supplier_id]
        alts = q(f"""SELECT supplier_id, status FROM sourcing WHERE part_id IN ({','.join(repr(x) for x in parts)})
                     AND supplier_id != '{r.supplier_id}'""")
        subj = r.subject.lower()
        kind = ("price_increase" if r.asked_pct else "index_clause" if "surcharge" in subj
                else "renewal" if "renewal" in subj else "capacity" if "capacity" in subj
                else "quality" if "escalation" in subj else "kit" if "kit" in subj
                else "rfq" if r.kind == "rfq" else "other")
        rows.append({
            "case": r.case, "type": kind, "supplier": r.supplier_id,
            "name": p["name"].iloc[0] if len(p) else "", "parts": r.part_ids,
            "asked_pct": r.asked_pct,
            "index_move_pct": round(f["index_move_pct"].mean(), 1) if len(f) else None,
            "margin_pct": round(f["margin_pct"].mean(), 1) if len(f) else None,
            "colour": p["colour"].iloc[0] if len(p) else None,
            "days_late": round(p["days_late"].iloc[0], 1) if len(p) else None,
            "signals": p["signals"].iloc[0] if len(p) else [],
            "alternatives": "; ".join(f"{a.supplier_id} ({a.status})" for a in alts.itertuples()),
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def negotiation_events():
    return q("""SELECT n.*, s.category, s.country FROM negotiation_history n
                JOIN suppliers s ON s.id = n.supplier_id""")


def main():
    docs = notes()
    prof = supplier_profiles(docs)
    fair = price_fairness()
    trig = triggers(docs, prof, fair)
    neg = negotiation_events()
    spend = q("""SELECT fiscal_year, category, SUM(spend_eur) spend,
                        SUM(CASE WHEN s.detail='full' THEN spend_eur ELSE 0 END) detailed
                 FROM spend_cube c JOIN suppliers s ON s.id = c.supplier_id GROUP BY 1, 2""")
    idx = q("""SELECT v.series_id, s.name, v.month, v.value FROM index_values v
               JOIN index_series s ON s.id = v.series_id WHERE v.month >= '2021-01'""")
    quotes = q("""SELECT q.*, r.purpose FROM quotes q JOIN rfqs r ON r.id = q.rfq_id""")

    for name, df in dict(profiles=prof, fairness=fair, triggers=trig, notes=docs).items():
        df.to_csv(OUT / f"{name}.csv", index=False)
    payload = {
        "profiles": prof, "fairness": fair, "triggers": trig, "negotiations": neg,
        "spend": spend, "index": idx, "quotes": quotes,
        "notes": docs[["id", "date", "kind", "supplier_id", "subject", "body", "signals"]],
    }
    payload = {k: json.loads(v.to_json(orient="records")) for k, v in payload.items()}
    payload["levers"] = LEVER
    (OUT / "explore.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload))

    pd.set_option("display.width", 250, "display.max_columns", 30, "display.max_rows", 100)
    print(prof[["id", "name", "country", "category", "spend_fy26", "colour", "otd_pct", "ppm",
                "days_late", "avg_asked", "avg_settled", "credit_change", "signals"]].to_string())
    print(trig.to_string())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    quotes = q("""SELECT id, quote_date date, 'quote remark' kind, supplier_id, 'Quote remark' subject,
                         remarks body FROM quotes WHERE remarks != ''""")
    news = q("""SELECT id, date, 'news' kind, supplier_id, headline subject, headline || '. ' || body body
                FROM news WHERE supplier_id != ''""")
    df = pd.concat([docs.drop(columns="file"), quotes, news], ignore_index=True)
    df["signals"] = [[k for k, pat in SIGNALS.items() if re.search(pat, b, re.I)] for b in df.body]
    return df''')
s=s.replace('''        kind = ("price_increase" if r.asked_pct else''','''        kind = ("price_increase" if pd.notna(r.asked_pct) else''')
s=s.replace('''            "alternatives": "; ".join(f"{a.supplier_id} ({a.status})" for a in alts.itertuples()),''','''            "margin_at_ask_pct": round((1 - f["full_cost_est"].mean() / r.asked_price) * 100, 1)
            if pd.notna(r.asked_price) and len(f) and f["full_cost_est"].notna().all() else None,
            "alternatives": "; ".join(sorted({f"{a.supplier_id} ({a.status})" for a in alts.itertuples()})),''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
